title: R/T
infotainment: Uconnect 5, 12.3-inch center touchscreen, 16-inch driver display, integrated EV navigation with charge route planning
adasStandard: Standard ADAS includes forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, lane-departure warning with lane-keep assist, and adaptive cruise control. Sources: https://cars.usnews.com/cars-trucks/dodge/charger-daytona ; https://www.cars.com/research/dodge-charger_daytona-2025/specs/
adasOptional: Optional Plus Group / Tech Package adds intersection collision assist, traffic sign recognition, surround-view camera, parking assist with automated parallel/perpendicular parking, and Active Driving Assist (hands-on Level 2 lane-centering + adaptive cruise). No hands-free highway driving system offered. Sources: https://www.edmunds.com/dodge/charger/2025/st-402063906/features-specs/
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard rear-view camera with dynamic gridlines. Surround-view 360-degree camera optional via Plus / Tech package. No high-resolution / multi-angle differentiator advertised over class average. Sources: https://www.edmunds.com/dodge/charger/2025/st-402063906/features-specs/
sideViewCameraNotes: Surround-view 360-degree camera available as part of optional Plus / Tech package. No Honda LaneWatch-style dedicated side-view turn-signal camera. No trailer view (Daytona not rated for towing). Sources: https://www.edmunds.com/dodge/charger/2025/st-402063906/features-specs/
subscriptionFeatures: Connect ONE (OTA updates, vehicle health, auto SOS, remote lock/unlock, basic nav, EV charging tools, recall notifications) included free for 10 years. Connect Wi-Fi PLUS in-car hotspot is a separately priced subscription. SiriusXM trial then paid. No subscription-gated horsepower, ADAS, heated seats, or other hardware features identified. Source: https://www.driveuconnect.com/ ; https://media.stellantisnorthamerica.com/newsrelease.do?id=25241
drmNotes: Core driving — propulsion, steering, braking, climate, infotainment local features — works fully offline. Connected services (remote start/unlock, vehicle health alerts, OTA updates, EV charging route planning, automatic SOS) require the embedded cellular modem and active Connect ONE subscription (included free for 10 years on MY2024+). Stellantis has issued multiple OTA-delivered recalls on the Daytona (instrument-cluster software, pedestrian-warning amplifier), demonstrating the car accepts remote software changes by default. Source: https://media.stellantisnorthamerica.com/newsrelease.do?id=25241 ; https://moparinsiders.com/stellantis-recalls-charger-daytona-ev-and-wagoneer-s-for-display-failure/
killSwitchNotes: No impaired-driving-detection kill switch fitted. The NHTSA IIJA / HALT Act rulemaking deadline was missed in 2024; outer statutory deadline pushed to November 2027. The Daytona ships with Uconnect 5 over-the-air update capability — Stellantis already uses OTA to deliver recall software (e.g., the 2026 instrument-cluster fix), so a future software-based driver-monitoring system could in principle be added by OTA. Source: https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/
knownIssues: Owner-reported issues on MY2024-MY2025 Daytonas include misaligned driver doors causing metal-on-metal contact, factory paint damage, intermittent passive-entry, Uconnect/Wi-Fi connectivity errors, exterior rear-hatch button failures, and driver seat position resetting. The R/T was axed for MY2026 after disappointing sales. Source: https://www.hotcars.com/2025-dodge-charger-daytona-pain-live-with-user-complains/
recalls: Recall 44C (2025): missing pedestrian-warning amplifier software, ~8,390 units MY2024-MY2025. Recall (2026, owner letters 2026-05-21): instrument-cluster software fault that can blank critical warning lights, ~20,271 units MY2024-MY2025. Both addressed via dealer software flash. Sources: https://moparinsiders.com/stellantis-recalls-charger-daytona-ev-and-wagoneer-s-for-display-failure/ ; https://moparinsiders.com/dodge-charger-daytona-recalled-for-missing-pedestrian-warning-sound/
stateIncentives: State BEV incentives vary widely. CA Clean Vehicle Rebate Project closed 2023; CA Clean Cars 4 All up to $12,000 for income-qualified retirees. CO offers $5,000 state tax credit for new EV purchase. NJ ZIP $4,000 + sales-tax exemption. NY Drive Clean Rebate up to $2,000. Massachusetts MOR-EV $3,500. Federal $7,500 credit ended for purchases after 2025-09-30; Stellantis is offering an equivalent $7,500 dealer-cash credit on Charger Daytona inventory while supplies last. Sources: https://electrek.co/2025/10/03/jeep-dodge-chrysler-vehicles-still-qualify-for-7500-ev-credit/ ; https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/ev-tax-credits

title: R/T
adasStandard: Standard ADAS includes forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, lane-departure warning with lane-keep assist, adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go, drowsy-driver detection, traffic sign recognition. Source: https://www.dodge.com/2025/hornet/specs.rt.html ; https://cars.usnews.com/cars-trucks/dodge/hornet-plug-in-hybrid
adasOptional: Optional Tech Package adds intersection collision assist, 360-degree surround-view camera, automated parking assist (parallel and perpendicular), and Level 2 hands-on highway driver assist. Source: https://www.edmunds.com/dodge/hornet/2025/plug-in-hybrid/
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard rear-view camera with dynamic guidelines. 360-degree surround-view camera available in optional Tech Package. Source: https://www.edmunds.com/dodge/hornet/2025/plug-in-hybrid/
sideViewCameraNotes: Surround-view 360-degree camera available in optional Tech Package. No dedicated side-view camera. No trailer-view (Hornet not rated for significant towing). Source: https://www.edmunds.com/dodge/hornet/2025/plug-in-hybrid/
subscriptionFeatures: Connect ONE included free 10 years. Connect Wi-Fi PLUS paid hotspot. SiriusXM trial + paid. No subscription-gated hardware features identified. Source: https://www.driveuconnect.com/
drmNotes: Core driving works fully offline. Uconnect 5 connected services (remote start/unlock, vehicle health alerts, OTA updates, automatic SOS, Dodge Connect) require active cellular and Connect ONE subscription (10 years free on MY2024+). Source: https://media.stellantisnorthamerica.com/newsrelease.do?id=25241 ; https://www.aventurachryslerjeepdodgeram.com/stellantis-debuts-advanced-uconnect-system-with-consumer-connected-services/
killSwitchNotes: No impaired-driving-detection kill switch fitted. Same regulatory backdrop as Charger Daytona: NHTSA HALT Act final rule outer deadline now November 2027. Hornet uses Uconnect 5 with OTA capability that could host a future software-based driver-monitoring system. Source: https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/
knownIssues: Owner forum reports note charging-port latch sticking in cold weather, occasional Uconnect 5 reboots, and powertrain control module software glitches affecting hybrid mode transitions. The car's discontinuation announcement (January 2026) creates long-term parts and service uncertainty despite Stellantis' stated commitment to ongoing support. Source: https://www.hornetowners.com/threads/dodge-hornet-and-all-other-stellantis-phev-models-officially-discontinued.1502/
recalls: Data unavailable: no Hornet-specific NHTSA recalls of major scale identified in research. Stellantis-wide Uconnect-related campaigns may apply to specific VIN ranges. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_Hornet
stateIncentives: Hornet R/T PHEV did not qualify for the IRA federal point-of-sale $7,500 credit because it is assembled in Italy (not final-assembled in North America). Stellantis is offering an equivalent $7,500 dealer-cash credit on remaining MY2025 Hornet R/T inventory through end-of-life. State-level: CO PHEV $1,500-$3,500 state tax credit; NJ ZIP rebate not applicable to PHEVs; MA MOR-EV $1,500 for PHEVs ≤$55k. Source: https://electrek.co/2025/10/03/jeep-dodge-chrysler-vehicles-still-qualify-for-7500-ev-credit/ ; https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/ev-tax-credits
tcoSource:
5-year TCO at 15,000 mi/yr for the Hornet R/T plug-in hybrid. Source priority: CarEdge (model-aggregated), KBB (2025 model-year), with R/T-PHEV-specific adjustments noted.

- Depreciation $26,387 — CarEdge Hornet ([caredge.com/dodge/hornet/costs](https://caredge.com/dodge/hornet/costs)). KBB 2025 model shows $19,859 — CarEdge used for conservative figure given PHEV battery-tied resale risk.
- Insurance $12,975 ($2,595/yr) — CarEdge Hornet.
- Maintenance $3,397 — CarEdge.
- Repairs $1,500 — PHEV-adjusted (higher than CarEdge baseline given complexity; Alfa Tonale shared powertrain). Dodge offers no complimentary maintenance.
- Fuel/electricity $7,800 — PHEV-adjusted from CarEdge's gas-Hornet $9,625. Assumes ~50% of 15k mi/yr driven on battery (33mi EV range, 77 MPGe combined; 29 MPG gas mode).
- Financing $6,903 — KBB 2025 ([kbb.com/dodge/hornet/2025/cost-to-own](https://www.kbb.com/dodge/hornet/2025/cost-to-own/)).
- Taxes & fees $4,500 — KBB-derived (KBB total $57,083 less above components).

Edmunds & KBB direct pages returned 403; figures sourced via search summaries and CarEdge fetch.

**Note**: Dodge Hornet R/T is rebadged Alfa Romeo Tonale PHEV. PHEV variant has higher fuel-cost sensitivity to charging behavior than pure-gas Hornet GT.

Primary: CarEdge (https://caredge.com/dodge/hornet/costs) — 5-year total $56,331; depreciation $24,030 (from $38,871 avg new price), insurance $13,210 ($2,642/yr), fuel $9,625 (27 MPG, 15k miles/yr), financing $6,068 (72mo @ 6.99% APR, 20% down), maintenance+repairs $3,397 combined (split ~60/40 to $2,038 maintenance / $1,359 repairs).
